<role>
You write a one-page opportunity brief for a Keelwater product manager. Keelwater makes claims-handling software. You use only the facts and customer insights below.
</role>
<opportunity>
{
 "title": "Integrations tab visible to all users",
 "problem_statement": "Junior staff see the integrations tab despite not needing access. This causes confusion among users who should not have that visibility."
}
</opportunity>
<fact_sheet>
{
 "as_of": "2026-11-03",
 "accounts_n": 1,
 "mentions_n": 1,
 "routes_n": 1,
 "mentions_by_route": {
  "sales": 1
 },
 "arr_total_gbp": 740000.0,
 "renewals_90d_n": 0,
 "accounts": [
  {
   "name": "Saltmarsh Specialty",
   "arr_gbp": 740000.0,
   "renewal_date": "2027-05-15",
   "mentions": 1
  }
 ]
}
</fact_sheet>
<insights>
[
 {
  "id": "636f7e5217dbdd0d",
  "quote": "can we adjust roles so only senior handlers see the integrations tab? It’s causing confusion.",
  "account": "Saltmarsh Specialty",
  "route": "sales",
  "date": "2026-09-26T14:35:00Z"
 }
]
</insights>
<rules>
- Cite every insight you rely on as [i:INSIGHT_ID], using the id exactly as given. Cite at least three different insights when three or more are given, and cover every route that appears.
- Use these sections, in this order, as Markdown headings: "## Problem", "## Who is affected", "## Evidence", "## Why now".
- Every bullet under "Who is affected" and "Evidence" ends with a citation. Every sentence that contains a number or a date carries a citation.
- Copy every account count, mention count, route count, renewal count and ARR figure from the fact sheet. Never compute, add up or round a number yourself; write an ARR figure only as it appears in the fact sheet, in pounds.
- Write counts as digits exactly as the fact sheet gives them ("5 accounts", never "five accounts"); never write "one customer" or "a single customer" unless the fact sheet count says 1 for that same thing.
- Put text in quotation marks only when it is a customer quote copied word for word, character for character, from one insight cited in the same sentence. Never put quotation marks around a paraphrase, a fragment of your own wording or a phrase from the fact sheet; when unsure, paraphrase without quotation marks.
- Name a customer only when a cited insight in the same sentence belongs to that customer.
- Do not claim more than the evidence shows: no "all customers", no scope wider than the cited accounts, and mention any cited insight that points the other way.
- Do not recommend a solution.
</rules>
<output>
JSON only: {"body_md": the brief as Markdown, "citations": the list of insight ids you cited}
</output>

response.content:
{"body_md": "## Problem

Junior staff can see the integrations tab even though they do not need access, and this visibility is causing confusion among users who should not have it [i:636f7e5217dbdd0d].

## Who is affected

- Saltmarsh Specialty, an account with 740000.0 GBP in ARR and a renewal date of 2027-05-15, raised this concern [i:636f7e5217dbdd0d].
- The request came through the sales route, which accounts for 1 mention across 1 route [i:636f7e5217dbdd0d].

## Evidence

- Across 1 accounts and 1 mentions, the only mention of this issue came from the sales route [i:636f7e5217dbdd0d].
- A user at Saltmarsh Specialty asked whether roles could be adjusted so that only senior handlers see the integrations tab, describing it as causing confusion [i:636f7e5217dbdd0d].
- There are 0 renewals in the next 90 days tied to this feedback [i:636f7e5217dbdd0d].

## Why now

- The feedback was logged on 2026-09-26, and the fact sheet is current as of 2026-11-03 [i:636f7e5217dbdd0d].
- Saltmarsh Specialty renews on 2027-05-15, so there is no renewal pressure inside the next 90 days [i:636f7e5217dbdd0d].
- No insight in the current set points the other way; the single mention is the only signal recorded [i:636f7e5217dbdd0d].
", "citations": ["636f7e5217dbdd0d"]}
